problem:
The responsiveness flow of 2026-10-25 took 7 h 26 min for 6 tasks and about $52: one declared reviewer (3.3 h waiting), a full check gate on every approval attempt, rules that combined into dead ends, and no view of where the time went. Every spec was built with the same ceremony whatever its risk, and nobody in the middle exercised judgement. The spec flow itself mixes decisions: 'propose' is only a readiness check that freezes the document, and 'approve' accepts the intent, creates the tasks and starts the flow in one click. A send-back rejects every piece of evidence the task had, with one reason, including the ones that held (requirement_evidence.decide_with_verdict), so the record cannot say which requirement actually failed, and per-model verdict counts mostly measure rounds times requirements. Separately, 23-25 October recorded worktree removal emptying the main checkout's node_modules (F1038), the mender stranding its own checkout, an operator's 'nothing merges' silently undone (F1016), and tasks nobody could close.

The night of 2026-10-26/27 (slice B's flow, 22:57 to 05:44, about $44): the mender cost $15.9 (36%), 30 of its 40 stalls the same review stall re-raised every five minutes after it gave up (F1048, fixed) and all 6 'loop stalled' stalls raised in the seconds before a review was dispatched (F1049). T2's ruff check failed 12 s after completion and QA was dispatched 26 s later to find the same two imports; three reviews (about 52 min of Opus) found only what the checks found. The project checks had no UI check, so a change with 24 failing vitest tests passed them. A timing test that also failed on main held QA's approval of T1 for 2 h 40 min while the operator slept, and the fix, filed outside the flow, sat assigned for 1.5 h because nothing starts a task outside a flow.

in_scope: Worktree and merge-target safety (F1038, mender checkout, F1016)
One explicit decision of who may move which task, at every level, with a test that no task can get stuck
Exploring ends at an approved plan: Check never freezes the document, the proposed phase is retired, approve accepts the plan, build is a separate action

Builds: a driver (Hub flow, lead agent, by hand), a gate level (Fast, Reviewed, Gated, with the evidence half of document rigor folded in), builders, a reviewer pool, a lead, budget, window and where the work lands
Amendments after approval proposed by the author and the lead and accepted by the operator
Each piece of evidence judged on its own in a verdict, with its own reason
The Hub noticing and raising main moving by anything other than its own integration
A merge queue so checks run once per batch
A redesigned spec page and side panel: native rendering, navigation, filtering, ordering (F1044), and the runs, cost and progress of each build
Project-wide stats from the same records, by spec, agent, model and level
A measured re-run comparing a slice-sized build with 2026-10-25
Overview notices, settings navigation and keyboard findings; runner rebind (F1023, F1024)
Checks before review: fast checks gate completion, review waits for the task's check run, a failed check returns the task without a review turn, and a UI check (slice L)

Failures that are not the task's own (failing on main too, or flaky) land with a recorded automatic override and a fix task at the head of the flow; tasks assigned outside a flow are started (slice M)
The mender's waking rules, default model and questions while the operator is away (slice N)
non_goals: Rewriting the engine: tasks, runs, worktrees, evidence and the transition table stay; only the policy of who may move what becomes explicit and configurable
A project-wide god agent: the mender stays a narrow maintenance role; the lead's authority is scoped to one build
Preventing agents from touching the main checkout: the Hub notices and raises it (operator, 2026-10-26), it does not block it
The Hub's own responsiveness: done by the 2026-10-25/26 overhaul

Changing the operator's rule that approval runs the checks: at every level red checks mean no merge, except slice M's automatic override, recorded on the transition, for a failure that is not the task's own (it fails on main at the same base, or passes rerun on its own), which slice D allows at Fast and Reviewed and never at Gated
Agents changing an approved spec directly: after approval every change is an amendment the operator accepts (operator, 2026-10-26)
Carrying evidence that held forward to the builder's next commit: deferred until slice H shows what re-recording costs (operator, 2026-10-26)

slices.done: The operator checks a document while an agent edits it, approval is refused once after the agent saves and accepted after reloading, the approved document shows its tasks as a plan with nothing running, and a build is then started from the page with the recommended settings filled in.

summary: Reworked 2026-10-26 after the operator's discussion of gate levels, the lead and the spec flow. The work converges on one idea: a spec is explored and checked while it is written, approved as a plan, and then built by one or more builds, each with a driver (the Hub's flow, a lead agent, or by hand), a level (Fast, Reviewed, Gated) and its people, while everything is recorded and shown on a redesigned spec page. After approval the author and the lead propose amendments, which the operator accepts. Each piece of evidence is judged on its own, so the record says which ones failed and why. Wave 1 runs A, B and C in parallel (disjoint code); K follows B; D follows B and C; E follows D; F is mocked now and wired as C and D land; H, the measured re-run, closes the roadmap. I and J stay independent. Amended 2026-10-27 after the night of 26/27 October, when slice B's flow took 6 h 47 min for 4 tasks: every send-back was something a check catches, three reviews ran beside checks that had already failed, one test failing on main too blocked every approval for 2 h 40 min, and the mender spent 36% of the cost re-raising one stall. Three slices are added and built first: L (checks run before anyone reviews) and N (the mender wakes only for real stalls) in Wave 0, M (a red main or a flake does not hold the night) after L. D is split in two: D (builds) and D2 (amendments, main watched, the next slice offered). Build order: Wave 0 L, N; Wave 1 A, C, K, M, I, J; Wave 2 D, then D2; Wave 3 E and F's wiring; Wave 4 G, then H. B is built.
title: Flows that do not stall: the work after the 2026-10-25 retrospective
